item.title: LOT-081: accounts and login screen
item.body:
LOT-081 — accounts and login screen ([spec](docs/lots/LOT-081-accounts-login.md)).

**Problem.** The app has engine login (LOT-043) and an account store (LOT-065) but no way to sign in, switch account or keep a session across launches.

**Cause.** Phase 4 app lot: the screens and the composition were not built yet.

**What changed** (all under `App/`, no engine change):
- `AccountsModel` (`@Observable @MainActor`): sole owner of one `HFRSession` per account, restored at launch from the stored cookies and `hash_check`; mirrors the credential store (an account whose Keychain write failed is never shown). Add (fresh session, becomes current, as legacy), log in again (the account's own session + `expectedUserKey`), select, remove (confirmation, no server logout, as legacy). Background avatar fetch through `AnonymousTransport`, `https://forum-images.hardware.fr` only, no redirect, ≤ 256 KiB.
- Session check seam `SessionChecking`: `LocalSessionCheck` today (no usable `md_user` → expired, nothing sent); LOT-044's `SessionRefreshFlow` plugs in as one adapter once #29 merges, and a `valid` result is already persisted.
- `LoginModel` + `LoginView` (AutoFill content types, cancel = cancelled login, password only in memory), `AccountsView`, `AccountMenuButton` (toolbar), `AccountMessages`: one actionable French text per `LoginError` / `NetworkError` / store case; a cancellation shows nothing. Store problems at launch (corrupted → erase on confirmation only; newer version → never overwritten; Keychain unavailable → retry).
- `SwiftHFRApp` creates the model, injects it and runs `restore()` in `.task`; `RootView` only gets the toolbar button.

**Why this wide.** Only the lot scope; the forum screens are LOT-082. Seam for #32: `AccountsModel.currentSession` (nil = logged out) is the session `AppEnvironment` should use, and `current?.id` the account name for the Q-7 rule; whichever PR merges second wires them and moves `AccountMenuButton` into the navigation toolbar (the conflict is limited to `SwiftHFRApp.swift` / `RootView.swift`).

**Tests** (`App/SwiftHFRTests/Accounts/`, Swift Testing, 33 new): restore (sessions rebuilt, expired identity kept not deleted, `valid` persisted, other outcomes write nothing, single restore under concurrency, corrupted/newer store), login (stored under `userKey`, every `LoginError` leaves store and session untouched, re-login uses own session + `expectedUserKey`, known account's session replaced only after a successful store write), select/remove, `LoginModel`, messages, avatar loader. Mutations run locally (single-restore guard, persist-after-valid, fresh session for a new account, `expectedUserKey`, avatar port check, no-redirect) each fail their tests.
Local: `xcodebuild build test` green on iPhone 18 Pro and iPad Pro 11-inch (M5), iOS 27.0 simulator; Release `generic/platform=iOS` unsigned build green.

The `App build + tests (iOS 27 simulator)` job is not a required check yet: adding it to the `dev-swift` ruleset is the repository owner's action (ADR 0012).

Account removal can leave the app browsing as the removed account if a storage read fails immediately after deletion. Normal switching has isolation controls, and the identified risk is confined to the affected device and failure path. **Retained concerns** - **Medium · security · inferred:** Account authority cleanup depends on a successful read after the storage mutation. The evidence does not establish cross-device compromise, arbitrary-host credential disclosure, or infrastructure privileges. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _inferred_ — The conditional path is successful current-account deletion, failure of the following storage read, unchanged navigation generation, and continued use of the cached authenticated environment. Storage failure is a prerequisite, not an attacker capability established by this review. This lifecycle coupling is introduced by the new account-bound composition. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The reused login engine validates the returned identity against the expected account and checks it again after the profile response before adopting credentials. HFRSession uses a separate ephemeral cookie jar per account, disables shared cache and credential storage, and restricts authenticated requests through its host policy. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Normal switching changes the session generation and constructs separate navigation models. Session-check completions verify that their session is still owned before applying results. The existing loader’s unstructured task can outlive caller cancellation, but its completion targets the old loader rather than the replacement navigation; this alone does not establish cross-account result delivery. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — Make removal invalidate the active navigation authority independently of a subsequent storage read. Publish the committed transition directly, or enter a fail-closed environment when publication fails, so successful credential deletion cannot leave a reusable authenticated screen. - _proposed_ — Before enabling the future network-backed checker, revalidate session ownership after awaited persistence reads and make identity-mismatch recovery withdraw the rejected session even if reloading stored credentials fails. **Check cancellation before the login is saved.** `AccountsModel.logIn` has no cancellation check after the login exchange returns. It suspends on `session.cookies()` and `session.hashCheck` before `store.save`. If the sheet is dismissed during those suspensions, the account is still saved. A new account also becomes the current account. `LoginModel.run()` then sets `didSucceed`. The fix stops the save when the task was cancelled.
Suggested fix
```diff let account = Account( pseudo: result.userKey, displayName: result.displayName, cookies: await session.cookies(), hashCheck: await session.hashCheck ) + if Task.isCancelled { throw .login(.network(.cancelled)) } let stored: Account ```

Fixed in d0346e3: `AccountsModel.logIn` now throws `.login(.network(.cancelled))` before saving when the task was cancelled, for a new account. A re-login is still saved, because `LoginFlow` has already renewed that session in memory (LOT-043) and the store must match it (spec, Edge cases). Test: `newAccountCancelledAfterTheLoginIsNotAdded`, which fails without the check.

** Minor** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win** **Restore the stored session before marking a mismatched refresh as expired.** When an injected checker returns `.valid` with an `md_user` for another account, `AccountBook.add` rejects the refreshed cookies before the store is written. The stored credentials remain intact, but the current catch maps the error to `.corrupted`. A status-only fix is insufficient. `currentSession` still reads `sessions[id]` without checking the status, so it can expose the mismatched session. Restore the stored session before setting `.expired`. This preserves the existing-account re-login flow, which requires `sessions[id]`.

+    case restored
+    /// Being checked.

+    /// Confirmed by a login or a session check.
+    case valid

+    case expired
+    /// The check could not reach the forum; the session is kept.

+
+/// An account as the screens show it: no cookie, no token.

+    /// The account's key (`Account.pseudo`, the `md_user` value).
+    let id: String
+    /// Name shown in lists and menus.
+    let displayName: String
+    /// The current account, whose session the app uses.
+    let isMain: Bool
+    /// Avatar, decoded once by the model.
+    let avatar: UIImage?
+    /// Session state.
+    let status: AccountSessionStatus

+    /// A new account, or a known one typed again (it is refreshed in place).
+    case newAccount
+    /// A known account whose session must be renewed; credentials of another account are refused.
+    case existing(id: String, displayName: String)
